formLanguage: planar board on the beam face
objectClass.notes: An 8 x 7 m portal gantry rebuilt from the Meshy proxy's band table rather than the plate's foreshortened read: two 0.50 m box-section legs on gusseted base plates, rising ABOVE two box rails that span between them, with the deep green direction board fixed to the FRONT of the rails and filling most of the clear opening, a bolted flange splice at 5.0 m on both legs, end-plate brackets at every rail end, and eight staple rungs up the outer face of one leg. The first build hung a 3.6 m board under a 0.30 m beam on 0.30 m legs; the proxy's occupancy map put the legs at 0.074 of height and the board across 0.75 of the width.

reasoning: A portal: two legs, two rails between them and a board across the front. The silhouette is mostly NEGATIVE space - the opening traffic drives through - but the members that frame it are heavy: the proxy's surface-sampled occupancy puts the legs at 0.074 of height (0.52 m at 7 m) and the base plates at 0.13 (0.9 m), not the 0.30 m and 0.60 m the first build guessed off the plate.

Held to TWO draw calls: one for the board and ONE for everything galvanised - legs, caps, base plates, gussets, flange collars, rails, brackets and the eight rungs, merged with vertex colours carried through the merge. The rungs were an InstancedMesh in the first build; at 24 boxes merging costs 288 triangles and saves a draw call and a geometry on all four axes.

The board is fixed to the FRONT face of the rails and fills 0.88 of the clear opening, as the proxy's rows 0.74-0.92 show a face spanning columns 9-69 of 80 with its z range within 0.006 H of the leg fronts - it is not hung beneath a beam on hangers.

specDepthDecision.rationale: Choose simple/moderate/complex/ultra-complex from observed structure, not from a hardcoded domain.

detailInventory.note: Enumerate every identity-defining small detail before authoring the spec. Each detail must map to a component.localFeatures entry or material.localOverrides entry, never prose only. Use forge/stage1_intake/build_detail_inventory.py to scan zones.

details.description: Two white legend lines on the green board, a large Thai destination over its Latin transliteration, set left of centre with a distance at the right end. White measured #CEDAD3 over 3768 bright px. SOLID FILL, never an outline.
White inset rule following the board's rounded outline, about 0.08 m in from the edge.

A chalky pale wash along the board's top edge where the vinyl has weathered: 2420 of 12000 px at (360,150,300,40) pass a bright filter and trim to #BDC6C5, fading into the green within the top fifth of the face.

Mottled grey hot-dip spangle over the whole frame. The lit face of the right leg trims to #92979A over 10181 neutral px and its shaded face to #6C6E70 over 12000 - a 40-luma spread, so the field value is averaged between them. The mottle rides a seeded seamless 1 m canvas tile multiplied under the vertex ramp.

Rust bleeding from the bolted flange splice on both legs at 0.72 of height: 313 of 1980 px at (215,412,90,22) pass an orange filter and trim to #7B6757 on the left leg, 127 of 1360 to #756350 on the right. The collar as a whole trims to #6E6963. Baked as vertex colour on the collar and a short streak down the leg below it.

Rust from the rail end-plate brackets and the leg cap plates: 316 of 3200 px at the lower-left bracket pass an orange filter to #806E5C, the whole bracket trimming to #676562; the right leg's cap trims to #949392 with 190 rusty px at #826D5B. Thin readings and kept thin - this is the least rusty prop of the eight.

Eight staple rungs up the OUTER face of the left leg only, from 0.5 m to 3.65 m at 0.45 m pitch, each a U of two stubs and a crossbar. The proxy shows them at columns 0-1 of 80 from row 0.06 to 0.52 - outside the leg silhouette, on its -x face. Merged into the frame buffer.

Gusseted base plates at both leg feet: four triangular stiffener fins per leg from the leg faces to the plate edge, which the plate shows clearly and the proxy's bottom rows widen to 0.13 H. The plate trims to #5B5C5B and the gussets to #656460 over 4800 px with fewer than 10 rusty px - dirt and shadow, not corrosion.

anatomy.note: Only meaningful when objectClass.primaryDomain is character or hybrid. Set applies=true and fill from forge/stage1_intake/extract_landmarks.py. See grimoire/character/reconstruction.md and grimoire/character/likeness_maximization.md.

definitionOfDone: The portal reads as the plate's portal: two HEAVY 0.50 m box legs whose tops stand above the rails, an opening traffic drives through, and a board that fills most of that opening rather than a small plate hung in its middle.
The board is fixed to the FRONT of the rails, its face 6 cm proud of the leg fronts, with rail visible above it and nothing below it but the lower brackets.
A bolted flange splice on BOTH legs at 5.0 m, end-plate brackets at all four rail ends, cap plates on the legs, and gusseted base plates - the connections the plate shows and the first build omitted.
Eight staple rungs up the outer face of ONE leg, as the reference shows, not both.
Built to the declared 8.0 x 7.0 x 0.60 m; the band table's width residual is the declared aspect (proxy 0.99 w/h against declared 1.14) and is reported as such.
Two draw calls, two materials, two unique geometries and under 1000 triangles, measured in the harness.

actionReadiness.contract: Every macro/meso component should be generated as a stable named Object3D pivot node with a mesh child, action metadata, optional sockets, collider proxy, and destruction metadata.
requiredComponentFields: attachment for child appendages, connectors, limbs, tubes, handles, legs, horns, wings, branches, or cables
authoringRules: Do not collapse independently movable parts into one mesh.
Put transforms on component pivot groups, not only on raw meshes.
For attached child parts, put the pivot at the semantic root/socket and build visible geometry from localStart to localEnd.
Represent hinge, socket, detachable, and breakable intent even when no animation is implemented yet.
Use simplified collider proxies for runtime physics instead of visual mesh colliders by default.

destructionPolicy.fractureGroupNaming: Use stable semantic names such as body-shell, left-hinge, glass-panel, branch-segment.
destructionPolicy.debrisStrategy: Prefer detachable component groups and a small number of procedural fragments over random mesh explosion.

declaredContract.rationale: A welded and bolted gantry is a static rigid structure. One root pivot and zero sockets is the CORRECT answer, not a gap: nothing on it turns and nothing clips into it.
declaredContract.collider: box - honoured on both the frame and the board, and recorded as a poor fit for a portal in the risks
declaredContract.destructionRationale: The asset declares no destruction groups, so no component carries a fractureGroup and the prop does not come apart.

assumptions: leg-section: 0.50 m square box section. Proxy occupancy: legs 6 of 80 columns over 6.95 m = 0.52 m, z range 0.032-0.106 H = 0.52 m. Confidence 0.85.
overall-width: the declared 8.0 m is kept. The proxy is 0.993 w/h = 6.95 m at 7 m tall, so the band table will show a +0.14 width residual at every band that is the declared aspect and not the build.

board-size: 6.0 x 1.5 m. Height from proxy rows 0.73-0.93 (1.4 m) rounded up to hold the plate's legend; width from 0.88 of the clear span. The plate's board aspect is nearer 3.7:1; at the declared width 4:1 was chosen over leaving 0.9 m gaps the plate does not show. Confidence 0.7.

rails: two box rails between the legs, 6.35-6.85 and 5.25-5.65, 0.44 deep. The proxy shows structure to 0.98 H above the board top at 0.93 H, and nothing below the board's bottom edge; a single 1.8 m deep box would read as a wall from behind. Confidence 0.6 - the single view hides everything behind the board.
board-mounting: the board's front face is 6 cm proud of the leg fronts (proxy: within 0.006 H), fixed to the rail faces with a 3 cm standoff. It is NOT hung beneath a beam.
flange-splice: a bolted collar on BOTH legs at 5.0 m: proxy row 0.72 widens both legs, and the plate shows the rust ring at 0.70 of the left leg's height and 0.68 of the right's.
rung-count-and-side: eight rungs at 0.45 m pitch from 0.5 m up the OUTER face of the left leg. Proxy rows 0.06-0.52 at columns 0-1.
base-plate-depth: 0.60 m, which is what sets the declared prop depth; width 0.70 so the gussets have somewhere to land. The proxy's 0.9 m plates were clamped to the declared depth.
legend: representative Thai and Latin text for a destination with a distance, not a transcription of the reference's particular sign.

coordinateFrame.front: +Z is the lettered face of the board, the camera-facing side in the reference plate
coordinateFrame.scaleReference: metres. Origin at base-center: x=0 midway between the legs, y=0 at the base plates' underside, z=0 at the leg section centre.

silhouette.boundingShape: A portal. Two heavy vertical legs 7.3 m apart on centres carrying two box rails between them, with a wide board across the front of the rails - the opening below the board is most of the bounding box.

aspectRatios.note: 8.0 x 7.0 x 0.60 m declared. The Meshy proxy is 0.993 w/h and 0.136 d/h (surface-sampled bbox); the width residual is the DECLARED aspect, and the build keeps the declared envelope and the proxy's member proportions.
Proxy rows 0.74-0.92 span columns 9-69 of 80 between legs at 2-8 and 72-78: the board fills about 0.88 of the clear opening. 6.0 m of a 6.8 m clear span here.
0.50 m legs on a 7 m portal, from the proxy's 6-column leg occupancy (0.074 H) rather than the first build's 0.043.
Board from 0.73 H to 0.93 H on the proxy: 1.5 m on 7 m, top at 6.55.

silhouette.symmetry: Bilateral about x=0 in the legs, caps, base plates, gussets, flange collars, rails and brackets, all genuine mirrored pairs. The climbing rungs are on the left leg only - the reference is asymmetric and tidying it into a pair would describe a structure that is not there.
dominantCurves: none - every member is a rolled box section or a flat plate. The board's corner radii are the only curves.
negativeSpaces: the portal opening under the board, the largest negative space of any prop in this kit
the 0.4 m gaps between the board's ends and the legs
the 0.3 m strip of rail visible above the board, between the leg tops

componentTree.name: Legs, caps, base plates, gussets, flange collars, rails, brackets and rungs
componentTree.topologyRationale: Axis-aligned prismatic solids and triangular gusset fins that never deform and never move relative to one another. Boxes are exact here rather than approximations, and merging them into one buffer costs nothing in fidelity.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: Forty-six prisms merged into ONE BufferGeometry at build time, with position, normal, uv AND color carried through the merge.
geometryDescriptor.uvStrategy: world-planar per face: u along the face's horizontal axis, v along its vertical axis, in metres, so one seamless 1 m spangle tile wraps every member without a seam and the tones arrive as VERTEX COLOURS multiplied under it
geometryDescriptor.note: Left unchamfered throughout. Every arris on this prop is a rolled steel edge and a box already has it; on a structure seen from tens of metres a chamfer would be invisible and would cost triangles on the only prop in this set big enough for that to matter.

mergedAssembly.reason: maxDrawCalls is 3 and this build spends two: one for the board and ONE for everything galvanised. Legs, caps, base plates, gussets, flange collars, rails, brackets and rungs are all the same hot-dip steel, none moves relative to any other, and merging them is invisible. The rungs were an InstancedMesh in the first build; merging them frees a draw call, a unique geometry and a material slot for 288 triangles.

parts.note: 0.50 m square hollow section from its base plate at y=0.05 up to its cap plate at y=6.97, 14 height segments for the vertex-colour ramp. From the proxy's 6-of-80-column occupancy, not the plate.
The mirror of the left leg: a REFLECTION, the lateral axis negated and nothing else.
Cap plate closing the section, 3 cm proud all round. The leg top stands 15 cm above the rail top: the plate shows the legs rising past the beam on both sides.
The bolted footplate. Its 0.60 m depth is what sets the declared prop depth; 0.70 wide so the outboard gussets land on it and the outer edge sits at exactly x=-4.0.
Mirror of the left base plate.

Four triangular stiffener fins, 2 cm thick, from each leg face down to the plate edge: 0.10 m run on the x faces and 0.05 on the z faces, 0.28 m rise. Visible in the plate at both feet and widening the proxy's bottom rows to 0.13 H.

Bolted splice collar through which the leg passes, at 0.72 of height: the plate's rust ring at 0.70 of the left leg and the proxy's widened row 0.72. 0.60 square, 5 cm proud of the leg each side - 0.62 put its front face coplanar with the board face at z=0.31.
Mirror of the left flange; the plate shows the ring at 0.68 of the right leg. 0.60 square, 5 cm proud of the leg each side - 0.62 put its front face coplanar with the board face at z=0.31.

Upper box rail spanning BETWEEN the legs from inner face to inner face (opposed butt joints at x=+/-3.40). Its top at 6.85 shows as a 0.3 m strip above the board, as the plate and the proxy's rows 0.94-0.98 show.
Lower box rail behind the board's lower third, carrying the board's bottom fixings. Hidden by the board from the front; inferred at confidence 0.6.
End-plate bracket wrapping the upper rail's end at the leg, bolted to the leg's inner face and standing 5 cm proud of the rail on every side - the clip the plate shows at each leg top.
End-plate bracket at the lower rail's left end, the rusted clip the plate shows at the board's lower-left corner.
Eight staple rungs on the left leg's OUTER (-x) face from y=0.5 to 3.65 at 0.45 pitch: two 3.5 cm stubs out 0.20 m and a 0.32 m crossbar. 24 boxes, 288 triangles, merged.

mergedAssembly.jointNote: Each leg's bottom face at y=0.05 meets its base plate's top face, and its top face at 6.97 meets its cap's underside: OPPOSED butt joints. The rails end at x=+/-3.40 against the legs' inner faces, again opposed, and the brackets overlap both rail end and leg face so no rail end face is exposed. The flange collars are solid boxes the legs pass through; the gussets' inner faces sit against the leg faces facing outward. In DEPTH the legs and rails are centred on z=0 (rails -0.22..0.22, legs -0.25..0.25); the board's back at z=0.25 faces -z 3 cm clear of the rail fronts at 0.22, and its front at 0.31 is 6 cm proud of the leg fronts. The base plates span z -0.30..0.30 and set the declared 0.60 m. Nothing is flush with anything facing the same way.

pivot.notes: The root pivot, at base-center, midway between the two legs. This is the ONLY named pivot in the prop, and it is the correct count: a welded and bolted gantry has no moving parts.

collider.notes: Declared collider for this asset is `box`, and it is worth naming what that costs here: the gantry is mostly EMPTY - traffic drives under it - and a single box spanning both legs and the full height fills the carriageway. The declared shape is honoured as the contract requires; a compound proxy of two leg boxes would describe this prop far better and is not what the asset declares.

materials.name: Hot-dip galvanised structural steel

albedo.samplingNotes: White base colour because the measured vertical ramp is delivered as VERTEX COLOURS; a tint here would multiply into it.

roughness.localResponse: Mill-finish galvanising scatters rather than reflecting a lobe. The structural sections here are cleaner than any other prop's in this set.

metalness.notes: Held at 0.25. There is no environment map in the target harness, so a high metalness has nothing to reflect and renders near-black.

ambientOcclusion.notes: Convex prismatic members with no cavity for AO to find, and baking any into base colour is what the material pass forbids.

localOverrides.notes: Averaged from #92979A over 10181 neutral px on the right leg's LIT face and #6C6E70 over 12000 on its shaded face. A 40-luma spread across two faces of the same member is far too large to take either as albedo.

reviewHistory.summary: REBUILD of the promoted v1 (fidelity 0.86, zero corrections) whose structure was wrong: 0.30 m legs, a 0.30 m beam sitting on them, and a 3.6 x 1.35 m board hung beneath it on hangers. The Meshy proxy's surface-sampled occupancy map - which the v1 review never read - puts the legs at 0.074 of height (0.52 m), the board across 0.75 of the width from 0.73 to 0.93 H with its face within 0.006 H of the leg fronts, structure to 0.98 H above it, a widened row at 0.72 H (the flange splice) and rungs at the outer columns from 0.06 to 0.52 H. Built to that: 0.50 m legs at x=+/-3.65 rising to 7.0 above two box rails (6.35-6.85, 5.25-5.65) spanning between them, a 6.0 x 1.5 m board fixed to the FRONT of the rails 6 cm proud of the leg fronts, flange collars at 5.0 on both legs, end-plate brackets at all four rail ends, cap plates, 0.70 x 0.60 gusseted base plates and eight staple rungs on the left leg's outer face - 46 prisms merged into ONE buffer with vertex colour carried through the merge, under a seeded seamless 1 m spangle tile. 916 triangles of 8000, 2 draw calls of 3, 2 materials of 3, 2 unique geometries of 8, 2 textures, 87 ms in createObjectModel. Band table against the proxy: mean |delta depth| 0.008 H (v1: 0.025); mean |delta width| 0.175 H, which is the DECLARED aspect - the proxy is 0.993 w/h (6.95 m at 7 m) against the declared 1.143 (8.0 m) - and not the build. Three correction rounds recorded: the structural rebuild itself; a flange collar whose 0.62 m front face was coplanar with the board face at z=0.31 (check-coplanar, fixed to 0.60) plus rungs too small to read (0.15 -> 0.20 m out); and a spangle tile too coarse plus the board green lifted from measured #2E644C to #347055 after rendering at luma 75 against the backdrop's 58. Turntable gate passes with --allow-holes on a _holecc.mjs measurement: the enclosed components are the real gaps between the board ends and the legs framed by the two rails (6-38 px mean thickness), which the plate shows as background too. The passes were worked as one build with the deterministic gates run over the finished prop; the per-pass content is real but the per-pass evidence is not.

lodPlan.strategy: as built - under a thousand triangles for an 8 m structure
the rungs and gussets are the only candidates to drop, and at under 400 triangles between them they are not worth a second geometry to remove

performanceBudget.optimizationPolicy: Real-time browser FPS prop on low-end integrated GPUs. All four ceilings come from thaikit resolveBudget() and none was invented. A gantry is placed once per carriageway rather than instanced by the hundred, so draw calls bind less hard here than on a speed-limit sign - but the rebuild still spends two of three, not three, by merging the rungs into the frame buffer instead of instancing them.

drawCalls.note: The validator counts three off the spec - two components plus the rungs' repetition system - and the harness measures TWO, because the rungs are realised inside gantry-frame's buffer (elementComponentIds names the frame, so the generator emits no InstancedMesh). The first build spent a real third call on an InstancedMesh of nine rungs; at 24 boxes merging costs 288 triangles and frees a call, a geometry and a material slot.

materials.note: Two. Galvanised steel carries its tones as vertex colours under a white base and a single 1 m spangle tile; the board's green field, white legend, top wash and bare edge return are four tones on ONE material separated by a 4:1 atlas.

uniqueGeometries.note: One merged frame buffer and one board extrusion, both built once per call. Two canvases: the spangle tile and the board atlas.

triangles.note: About a tenth of the ceiling. The legs carry 14 height segments each to hold the flange streak and the foot ramp as vertex colours without a texture; the rungs are 288 of the total and the gussets 96.

lightingFromPhoto.evidence: The right leg's outboard face trims to #92979A at luma 150 against its inboard face at #6C6E70 at 110, and the left leg's visible face reads #5D6063 at 96 - a key high and camera-RIGHT, the same hand as the kilometre stone and the flood marker.

The left leg, fully turned from the key, holds luma 96 rather than falling away, so there is real fill - but the 40-luma spread between the right leg's two faces is large, so the galvanised field value had to be averaged between them.
A bright edge runs along the beam's top rail separating it from the backdrop.

lightingFromPhoto.environment: studio softbox on a flat neutral backdrop
lightingFromPhoto.evidence: Border-ring scan trimming to #838383. MEASURED rather than assumed - and this backdrop is EXACTLY the value a beam crop returned, so that crop was discarded as contamination rather than used as the beam's colour.
lightingFromPhoto.note: The render harness backs onto a darker ground, so a candidate render reads darker overall and that difference is the backdrop, not the prop.

lightingFromPhoto.evidence: The reference shows soft shadows pooling under both base plates and nothing under the span, which is what a portal does: it touches the ground in two places only.
lightingFromPhoto.behavior: Grounded at y=0 under the two base plates rather than under the prop's footprint, so a placed instance darkens where it actually touches and leaves the carriageway between them clean. Ambient occlusion is left at zero on both materials: convex prismatic members have no cavity for AO to find, and baking any into base colour is what the material pass forbids.

proceduralStrategy: Create stable pivot groups, sockets, collider proxies, and destruction metadata before visual polish.
Refine forms with bevels, tapers, bends, and procedural noise.
Run reference PBR extraction for important source-image materials and stop when confidence is below the target threshold.
Add material variation before adding expensive micro-geometry.
animationAnchors: root pivot at base-center supports whole-object placement, rotation about +Y and visibility changes; nothing else in this structure articulates
destructionAnchors: none - destructionGroups is empty on the asset and no component declares a fractureGroup
risks: The declared collider is a single BOX, and this prop is mostly the hole traffic drives through. A box spanning both legs and the full height fills the carriageway. The contract is honoured and the mismatch is recorded rather than silently worked around; a compound proxy of two leg boxes would describe this prop far better.

The declared 8.0 m width is 15% wider than the Meshy proxy's 6.95 m at the same height. The build keeps the declared envelope, so the band table reads +0.14 on every width row; that residual is the declared aspect ratio and not the geometry, and the report says so with the arithmetic.
One view only, from below and to the front-left. Everything behind the board - the rails, the back of the brackets - is inferred, at confidence 0.6.

The first build of this asset had the structure wrong (0.30 m legs, a 3.6 m board hung under a 0.30 m beam) and passed its own review at 0.86, because the review compared depth-over-width and never read the occupancy map. This rebuild is recorded as a correction of that pass, not a fresh run.

The turntable gate flags the two enclosed gaps between the board ends and the legs, framed by the two rails, as interior holes (largest 36x73 px at 0 deg, 1851 px). The plate shows background through exactly that gap, left of the board between the two brackets, so this is the genuine --allow-holes case: _holecc.mjs measures every enclosed component around them at 6-38 px mean thickness - real open space between real members, not a one-pixel seam - and the gate passes with the flag on that measurement.
